title: Neo-Assyrian Empire
summary: The Neo-Assyrian Empire, the last phase of Assyrian power, began with the reign of Adad-nirari II in 912 BCE, who retook lost lands and deported defeated Aramaeans into the Assyrian heartland. Later kings extended it across Mesopotamia, the Levant, Anatolia and parts of Persia; Sennacherib took Israel and Judah, and Esarhaddon conquered Egypt. Ashurbanipal gathered a vast library at Nineveh. Revolts followed his death in 627, and in 612 BCE Medes and Babylonians sacked Ashur, Kalhu and Nineveh; a last king held out at Harran.

uncertainty.note: WHE dates the empire 912-612 BCE; the EBSCO king list gives Adad-nirari II c. 911-891. After the capitals fell, the last king held out at Harran.

as_recorded.value: In 612 b.c., however, Assyria s capital, Nineveh , was besieged and destroyed

where.modern_name: Nineveh, Mosul, Iraq (last capital; stand-in pin for the empire)

importance.justification: The first empire to rule from Mesopotamia to Egypt, for three centuries (R3 D3 T3 L3).

related.because: The 612 BCE sack of Nineveh marked the catastrophic military collapse of the Neo-Assyrian imperial core.
Sennacherib's siege of Lachish was a major campaign demonstrating Assyrian imperial siegecraft in the Levant.
Ashurbanipal ruled the empire at its territorial and cultural zenith, creating the famous royal library at Nineveh.

reviewer_note: Coordinator review 2026-11-12: 911 as the empire start and the standing-army claim were on no cited page; added WHE Neo-Assyrian Empire (912-612 BCE) and rewrote summary and beats to it, EBSCO and Encyclopedia.com. Encyclopedia.com credits the sack of Nineveh to Medes, Scythians and Chaldeans; WHE to Medes, Babylonians and Persians. The 1-3 year tail covers the Harran remnant (EBSCO). Fall of Nineveh, Lachish and Ashurbanipal records linked.
